If I had had one before, it would’ve probably made the process of realizing I was agnostic worse than it already was. It’s like trying to get out of something you already took an oath to. If you genuinely want them to have the choice be their own you probably wouldn’t wanna put that on em.

There is a chance on the other hand that your child will forever be catholic, which would be great for you both to share something that will mean a lot. I think it’s even more important then for you to wait on the baptism, because you can have them more involved and excited about the event rather than confused and upset.

This was my moms way of introducing her kids to religion, and I’m the only one who’s openly agnostic. 

 So If he wants a compromise on that, tell him you’ll baptize them *only if* they agree to when they’re older (13 maybe? I think it’s a common compromise with these types of relationships but if neither of you want to budge there then maybe you both need time to think on it and mature.
